title: RcppTrust: A Thread-Safe C++ Trust Region Optimizer
text: RcppTrust::trust() drop-replacement trust::trust(). arguments, defaults, return value, implements exact algorithm: Newton / easy-easy / hard-easy / hard-hard case split trust-region subproblem, accept/reject radius-adjustment rule, termination criteria. Everything already know trust::trust() – objfun contract (return list value, gradient, hessian, list(value = Inf)/list(value = -Inf) signal infeasible point), rinit/rmax/parscale/iterlim/fterm/mterm/ minimize/blather arguments, shape returned list, blather = TRUE’s extra argpath/steptype/rho/… components – applies unchanged. 10 upstream’s tests/*.R scripts ported package’s test suite pass C++ core.
code: library(RcppTrust)  # Rosenbrock's function, exactly the example from ?trust::trust objfun <- function(x) {   f <- expression(100 * (x2 - x1^2)^2 + (1 - x1)^2)   g1 <- D(f, "x1"); g2 <- D(f, "x2")   h11 <- D(g1, "x1"); h12 <- D(g1, "x2"); h22 <- D(g2, "x2")   x1 <- x[1]; x2 <- x[2]   list(     value = eval(f), gradient = c(eval(g1), eval(g2)),     hessian = rbind(c(eval(h11), eval(h12)), c(eval(h12), eval(h22)))   ) }  out <- trust(objfun, c(3, 1), 1, 5) out[c("value", "argument", "converged", "iterations")] #> $value #> [1] 5.165437e-15 #>  #> $argument #> [1] 1 1 #>  #> $converged #> [1] TRUE #>  #> $iterations #> [1] 21

code: library(microbenchmark)  # same Rosenbrock objfun as above: 2 parameters, ~20 iterations mb_small <- microbenchmark(   trust = trust::trust(objfun, c(3, 1), 1, 5),   RcppTrust = RcppTrust::trust(objfun, c(3, 1), 1, 5),   times = 50 ) print(mb_small) #> Unit: microseconds #>       expr      min       lq      mean    median       uq      max neval #>      trust 1315.790 1346.505 1513.3728 1371.9080 1431.432 3615.334    50 #>  RcppTrust  585.022  606.494  632.8901  622.7625  664.459  699.822    50 d <- 30 mu <- seq_len(d) barrier_objfun <- function(x) {   normxsq <- sum(x^2)   omnormxsq <- 1 - normxsq   if (normxsq >= 1) return(list(value = Inf))   f <- sum(x * mu) - log(omnormxsq)   g <- mu + 2 * x / omnormxsq   B <- 4 * outer(x, x) / omnormxsq^2 + 2 * diag(d) / omnormxsq   list(value = f, gradient = g, hessian = B) }  r1 <- trust::trust(barrier_objfun, rep(0, d), 1, 100) r2 <- RcppTrust::trust(barrier_objfun, rep(0, d), 1, 100) # same solution, different number of steps to get there (see above) c(trust_iterations = r1$iterations, RcppTrust_iterations = r2$iterations) #>     trust_iterations RcppTrust_iterations  #>                   16                   16 max(abs(r1$argument - r2$argument)) #> [1] 2.775558e-17  mb_large <- microbenchmark(   trust = trust::trust(barrier_objfun, rep(0, d), 1, 100),   RcppTrust = RcppTrust::trust(barrier_objfun, rep(0, d), 1, 100),   times = 30 ) print(mb_large) #> Unit: microseconds #>       expr      min       lq      mean   median       uq      max neval #>      trust 1893.760 1956.123 2232.0896 1993.378 2691.718 2851.156    30 #>  RcppTrust  667.144  724.218  823.3094  861.798  902.655  964.977    30

title: RcppTrust: A Thread-Safe C++ Trust Region Optimizer
text: RcppTrust’s shared library never linked directly. Instead – following header-, positionally-indexed function-pointer pattern already used across nlmixr2 ecosystem (rxode2, n1qn1, lbfgsb3c) – consumer resolves trust_solve_c/trust_result_free function pointers , load time. full wiring three pieces, example reproduces single self-contained file demonstration. Add RcppTrust DESCRIPTION’s LinkingTo (header) Imports (R-level .RcppTrustPtr() getter). one translation unit, include registration header package-unique renaming #define generated init function doesn’t collide consumer’s: package’s .onLoad(), resolve pointers : , trust_solve_c_ptr trust_result_free_ptr live function pointers signatures trust_solve_c()/trust_result_free(), usable anywhere package’s C++ – including inside OpenMP loop fitting many subjects’ problems parallel: example whole pattern collapsed one file run live, via Rcpp::sourceCpp(), exactly work split across real package’s src/init.c, R/zzz.R, wherever fit happens: Note compiled file never links RcppTrust’s shared library – LinkingTo/Rcpp::depends() adds inst/include directory compiler’s include path. Every trust_* symbol used except two resolved pointers (trust_solve_c_ptr, trust_result_free_ptr) type macro, function call, exactly point: nothing creates ABI dependency specific build RcppTrust, stable, append-pointer table publishes.
code: extern "C" { #define iniRcppTrustPtrs _mypkg_iniRcppTrustPtrs #include <RcppTrust.h> iniRcppTrust } .onLoad <- function(libname, pkgname) {   .Call(`_mypkg_iniRcppTrustPtrs`, RcppTrust:::.RcppTrustPtr(), PACKAGE = "mypkg") } #pragma omp parallel for for (int i = 0; i < nSubjects; i++) {   trust_options_t opts = trust_options_default(1.0, 5.0);   trust_result_t res;   trust_solve_c_ptr(n, parinit[i], subject_objfun, &subjectData[i], &opts, &res);   // ... use res.argument, res.value, res.converged ...   trust_result_free_ptr(&res); } cpp_code <- ' // [[Rcpp::depends(RcppTrust)]] #include <Rcpp.h>  extern "C" { #define iniRcppTrustPtrs _vignette_iniRcppTrustPtrs #include <RcppTrust.h> iniRcppTrust }  // A thread-safe C objective function: Rosenbrock again, this time // filling value/gradient/hessian directly instead of returning a list. extern "C" int rosenbrock_c(int n, const double *par, double *value,                              double *gradient, double *hessian, void *ud) {   double x1 = par[0], x2 = par[1];   double t = x2 - x1 * x1;   *value = 100.0 * t * t + (1.0 - x1) * (1.0 - x1);   gradient[0] = -400.0 * x1 * t - 2.0 * (1.0 - x1);   gradient[1] = 200.0 * t;   hessian[0] = -400.0 * x2 + 1200.0 * x1 * x1 + 2.0;   hessian[1] = hessian[2] = -400.0 * x1;   hessian[3] = 200.0;   return 0; }  // [[Rcpp::export]] Rcpp::List fit_rosenbrock(SEXP ptrTable, Rcpp::NumericVector parinit) {   // normally done once, in .onLoad() -- see above   _vignette_iniRcppTrustPtrs(ptrTable);    trust_options_t opts = trust_options_default(1.0, 5.0);   trust_result_t res;   trust_solve_c_ptr(parinit.size(), parinit.begin(), rosenbrock_c, nullptr, &opts, &res);    Rcpp::List out = Rcpp::List::create(     Rcpp::_["argument"] = Rcpp::NumericVector(res.argument, res.argument + res.n),     Rcpp::_["value"] = res.value,     Rcpp::_["converged"] = res.converged != 0,     Rcpp::_["iterations"] = res.iterations);   trust_result_free_ptr(&res);   return out; } ' Rcpp::sourceCpp(code = cpp_code)  fit_rosenbrock(RcppTrust:::.RcppTrustPtr(), c(3, 1)) #> $argument #> [1] 1 1 #>  #> $value #> [1] 5.165437e-15 #>  #> $converged #> [1] TRUE #>  #> $iterations #> [1] 21

Geyer’s CRAN package trust, built use nlmixr2est. implements exact algorithm – Newton / easy-easy / hard-easy / hard-hard trust-region subproblem, termination criteria – exposes three ways: trust(), drop-R replacement trust::trust(), arguments, defaults, return value. trust_solve_c(), thread-safe C entry point (C objective function pointer plus small options struct, R API calls) safe call parallel C++ code OpenMP loop. header-, positionally-indexed function-pointer table (inst/include/RcppTrust.h), another package can call trust_solve_c() without linking package’s shared library – pattern rxode2/n1qn1/lbfgsb3c use across nlmixr2 ecosystem. See vignette("RcppTrust") ’s upstream trust, ’s different, worked example C interface registration pattern. Note package generated help AI (Claude/Gemini).
